key_insight: Reformulates tokenisation as a convex optimisation problem (a linear program) instead of using greedy subword merges, producing globally consistent vocabularies; ConvexTok improves intrinsic tokenisation metrics and lowers bits-per-byte (BpB).
problem_solved: Greedy tokenisers (e.g., BPE, Unigram) make locally optimal decisions that can produce suboptimal vocabularies and less efficient representations; the paper addresses the need for a principled, global optimisation for vocabulary construction.
method: Formulate vocabulary construction as a linear program (convex relaxation) that jointly optimises token selection and encoding costs.
Solve the convex relaxation with standard optimisation tools to obtain a continuous solution, then recover a discrete vocabulary (ConvexTok) via rounding/selection.
Evaluate ConvexTok against greedy baselines on intrinsic tokenisation metrics and bits-per-byte (BpB) to demonstrate consistent improvements.
impact: Offers a principled alternative to greedy tokenisers that can yield better compression and more coherent vocabularies, improving efficiency for model inputs and pre-processing pipelines; easily adopted by practitioners as a drop-in tokeniser construction method.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: Greedy pipeline (BPE/Unigram merges) vs ConvexTok pipeline (LP formulation → solver → rounding).
Flowchart of ConvexTok steps: objective setup, convex optimisation, continuous solution, discrete vocabulary recovery.

paper_authors: Jan Tempus, Philip Whittington, Craig W. Schmidt, Dennis Komm, Tiago Pimentel
